div.style: color: rgb(70, 88, 106) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
The model does not fit on the device.
Is that a dead end?

div.style: color: rgb(94, 61, 18) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
No. It is a RESIDENCY problem, not a capacity wall.
The question becomes: which bytes must be resident
RIGHT NOW, and which can be somewhere colder?

div.style: color: rgb(59, 42, 94) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
Tier 0 — device-resident
the hot set: current layer weights, live KV

div.style: color: rgb(59, 42, 94) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
Tier 1 — host DRAM
the rest of the weights, paged in on demand

div.style: color: rgb(59, 42, 94) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
Tier 2 — host DRAM staging ring
dirty pages coalesced before write-back

div.style: color: rgb(59, 42, 94) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
Tier 3 — NVMe
the cold store, bounded by SSD endurance

div.style: color: rgb(27, 58, 102) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
The activated-expert insight:
a frontier mixture-of-experts checkpoint activates
a small fraction of its experts per token.
STORED bytes minus ACTIVATED bytes = the opportunity.

div.style: color: rgb(27, 58, 102) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 120px; text-align: center; width: 120px;

span.p:
A memoizer is not a cache.
No budget, no victim, no accounting —
so residency grows monotonically
until the machine runs out.
